POV: In 2008 you put **$10,000** in
the S&P 500 VS gold
footer: S&P 500 with dividends · gold year-end price

verdict.text:
Gold led for 6 years.
Stocks won by **≈ $14,200**.

notes: $10,000 each at the Dec 31, 2007 close; V(y) = V(y-1) × (1 + r(y)); a point at y + 0.99 is the Dec 31 close of year y. Returns as sourced in teasers/v2/checks/04-chart-race.py (S&P 500 total return; gold year-end % change, 2025 = 4,319.37 / 2,624.60 − 1 = +64.57%). Finals: S&P 500 $65,995.78 → ≈ $66,000 (×6.5996 → ≈ ×6.60, log2 = 2.722 → ≈ 2.7 doublings); gold $51,791.18 → ≈ $51,800 (×5.1791 → ≈ ×5.18, log2 = 2.373 → ≈ 2.4); gap $14,204.60 → ≈ $14,200. 2008: S&P 500 −37.00% ($6,300.00), gold +5.6%. Gold end-2012 $20,107.76 (×2.01: doubled). Gold 2013 −28.0%. The lines meet at end-2013 ($14,374.72 vs $14,477.59) and cross at x ≈ 2014.04 (t ≈ 11.0 s): gold led ≈ 6 years; the S&P 500 leads at every year-end 2014-2025. 2022 S&P 500 −18.11% (≈ 18%); 2025 gold +64.57% (≈ 65%) closes the gap from $24,515 to $14,205. Race x 2008.0 → 2025.99 over t −0.4 → 33.6 s (≈ 1.89 s a year): frame 1 is already 0.2 years into the 2008 crash.
